sourceWindows: CURRENT / SHALL NOT FADE: https://groovearmada.bandcamp.com/album/body-action and https://daily.bandcamp.com/essential-releases/essential-releases-september-4-2026 — Groove Armada — Gangsta Girl retained from an August 21, 2026 EP; official text documents minimal percussion, ragga vocals, bassline and deconstructed dancefloor construction.

CURRENT / KALAHARI OYSTER CULT: https://ra.co/reviews/36353 — Reptant — Future Proof retained from May 2026 exact electro context: syncopated percussion, sparse instrumentation and a contorted acid line.

ADJACENT / CLUB ROMANTICO: https://ra.co/reviews/34912 — Bitter Babe & Nick León — Tranki retained from exact doubling/tripling drum construction and a late bassline change inside technoid club music.
ADJACENT / WERKDISCS: https://ra.co/reviews/12358 — Actress — Voodoo Posse Chronic Illusion retained from a clicky garage beat emerging in the second half and a stumbling rather than straight swing.
OVERLOOKED / ILIAN TAPE: https://ra.co/reviews/20887 — Skee Mask — Palo Alto and Kordman Return (Swing Mix) retained from sudden pattern shifts and exquisitely swung broken beats.

OVERLOOKED / LIMITED NETWORK: https://ra.co/reviews/35887 — Max Watts — The Silver Lining and Max Watts & Huey Mnemonic — Echoes Of Change retained from housey swing, a spinback breakdown and staccato drum programming.
OVERLOOKED / DEADPLATE: https://ra.co/reviews/11977 — Hodge — Turmoil retained from lithe two-step suggestion returning to deep-sub foundation.

FRESHNESS CHECK: exact repository searches found none of the nine track titles in current or archived STRANGE GAIT history; canonical, rejected, parked, retained and unresolved identities from prior runs were excluded.
explorationReceipt.approximateInspectedScope: Approximately 43 named tracks and releases across September/August/May 2026 current windows, adjacent house/electro/club material and overlooked 2012–2023 techno/bass catalogue reviews; metadata and attributed descriptions only; no audio audition.
exclusions: All canonical identities, active placement-specific rejects, untriggered PARKED revisits, previously retained exact identities and previously unresolved leads without materially new identity evidence were excluded.
The two listener-protected internal trio handoffs remain unavailable; Truth in Noise → Transparency and all other boundaries are not protected by implication.
Four consecutive ADDs and the 18-track / approximately 1h48m journey were treated as cumulative cost, not as an automatic moratorium.
Current sources with only release-level atmosphere, prestige, genre tags or no exact-track identity were inspected but not promoted.
No energy, density, perceived pulse, phrase structure, mixability or half/double-time relation was inferred.
Nine honest contenders survived; the request uses the full allowance because each clears the lead floor, not to satisfy a quota.
rankedLeadSummary: 1. Reptant — Future Proof: current electro contender with syncopated percussion and acid-line contortion; tests a deliberate different-world boundary.
2. Bitter Babe & Nick León — Tranki: adjacent technoid club contender whose drums double or triple and whose bassline changes late; tests an unprotected threshold or overture.
3. Skee Mask — Palo Alto: overlooked pacy techno with sudden pattern shifts; tests whether a compact early deviation earns another opening stage.
4. Groove Armada — Gangsta Girl: current deconstructed house contender with minimal percussion, ragga vocals and bassline; tests an adjacent afterword.
5. Max Watts — The Silver Lining: overlooked Detroit/tech-house swing with a spinback breakdown; tests a subtle early continuation or afterword.
6. Skee Mask — Kordman Return (Swing Mix): overlooked broken-beat swing and delay contender; tests the central slower-pulse passage.
7. Max Watts & Huey Mnemonic — Echoes Of Change: incremental minimal construction with staccato drums; tests the unprotected pre-trio threshold.
8. Hodge — Turmoil: overlooked lithe two-step-to-sub foundation; tests a central reset without relying on BPM.
9. Actress — Voodoo Posse Chronic Illusion: clicky garage beat enters in the second half and stumbles rather than swings cleanly; tests an overture or afterword.
